scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: Two independent falsifications. The narration's 'the same record is what the supply chain moves against' points at a contract with a different tender, quantity and unit price than the award just shown: the header reads '45,000 cartons RUTF delivered to Maiduguri · awarded under RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q2 2026' at USD 42.10, while the viewer has just watched a Q3 2026 award of 60,000 cartons to the same supplier at USD 42.29. Same supplier, same commodity, same city, tender names differing by one character. And the payoff 'nobody can trace a dollar to a carton' is spoken over a DISBURSED field reading USD 0.00.
fix_recommendation: Either create and open the contract produced by the on-camera Q3 award, or add an explicit clause to the narration naming this as an earlier award on the same corridor already in execution. The recipe's own 'show' text already says 'not the one just made' — that disclosure never reaches the viewer.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The five-second read is 'a contract for Savanna Nutrients, $1.89M obligated, nothing disbursed' — wrong on both axes the scene needs: that this is the contract just awarded, and that money has moved. The record's parts are well labelled (the 'The appropriation this contract obligates money from' subtitle is genuinely good plain English), so what it IS lands; the why does not.
fix_recommendation: Open the contract on the demonstrated award, or narrate the substitution; and stage the closing frame on a contract where obligated -> disbursed -> delivered cartons is a visible chain rather than a zero.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The DISBURSED card states its own rule — 'AGAINST CONFIRMED DELIVERY ONLY' — and reads USD 0.00 directly above twelve consignments with status Delivered. Verified in the model: disbursed_value = confirmed_quantity x unit_price, and _quantity_in_contract_unit counts only legs ARRIVING at the contract's delivery place (Maiduguri). The Delivery schedule card therefore lists hub-to-centre legs out of Maiduguri that by construction can never move the disbursed figure, plus consignments to Gombe and Damaturu under a contract headed 'delivered to Maiduguri'. Delivered quantities in the visible column also sum well above the card's own footer figure of '15,000 confirmed at destination'.
fix_recommendation: Group the Delivery schedule into 'inbound against this contract' vs 'onward distribution past the delivery point', and distinguish Confirmed from Delivered in the status column, so the delivered rows reconcile to the stated confirmed figure and the disbursement rule is legible.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: Spine item S5 is grounded in real code (models/execution.py — Contract created from an Award, drawing against an Appropriation), and funder/appropriation/IATI id/obligated are all on screen. But the concept_claim's operative words — 'the same record the tender produced' — have nothing on screen linking this contract to any award: 'awarded under RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q2 2026' is dead plain text.
fix_recommendation: Render the 'awarded under ...' line as a link to the award record, so the continuity claim is demonstrable on screen rather than narrated.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The 'Drawn against' grid wraps DISBURSED and UNIT PRICE to a second row leaving a large dead right half; OBLIGATED USD 1,894,500.00 carries no more typographic weight than the FUNDER label beside it; and the caveat that resolves the whole 0.00 contradiction is the lowest-contrast text on the card.
fix_recommendation: Promote OBLIGATED and DISBURSED to a paired hero treatment side by side with the 'against confirmed delivery only' rule at readable contrast, and rebalance the grid so the six fields sit on even rows.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: All 8 actions ok and the captured frame is the legible result of a real effecting click. But the schedule's reconciliation footer — '45,000 cartons contracted · 15,000 confirmed at destination · 30,000 outstanding. Status and quantities are derived from the event log, not entered.' — is the literal proof of the narrated payoff and never enters frame during the 3.2s closing hold.
fix_recommendation: Add a scroll_to on the modal's reconciliation footer inside the closing hold so the payoff line is on screen while it is narrated.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: Scored once for the whole walkthrough, attached to the climax. The rewritten cost claim is TRUE — the split as awarded (USD 3,374,400, USD 42.18/carton) is USD 81,000 / USD 1.01 per carton cheaper than the cheapest single-supplier consolidation (Savanna, USD 3,455,400, USD 43.19/carton) — but that is exactly the problem for this dimension. Because the resilient split is also the cost minimum, the scene demonstrates no trade-off: greedy cheapest-per-lot reaches the identical answer, and the narration's own stated failure mode (concentrating a four-country response on the cheapest single bidder) is never instantiated, because concentrating is dearer here. Calling it 'the decision the lot structure exists to make possible' overstates what the data makes it: an automatic optimum. Steelman kept: the split does avoid a dominated outcome that would be both dearer and concentrated.
fix_recommendation: Re-price the fixture so the resilient split genuinely costs something — make one supplier cheapest on BOTH corridors (e.g. Savanna bids ~41.50 into Djibo) so consolidating would be ~USD 60-90k cheaper and Ada is visibly paying a premium for corridor independence. Alternative: keep the data and soften the narration so it claims only that per-lot award avoids a dearer, concentrated outcome. Concept gate — do not auto-apply.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: The award state machine is coherent (Award click -> badge + buttons removed + toast, proven by the before/after pair). But a single click commits USD 2,537,400 with no confirmation and no visible undo, and no award criterion is stated anywhere — price and technical are both shown with no combined score or weighting, so the audience's actual decision ('is this defensible?') is unsupported.
fix_recommendation: Add a confirm step on Award naming lot, supplier and lot value, and surface the evaluation rule on the lot header (a combined score column, or an explicit 'lowest compliant price, technical >= 70' line).

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: Tables are tight and currency formatting is consistent, but technical scores are all rendered in the same accent green (60 styled identically to 91) and read as links though they are not, the column has no stated scale, and after award the Award-button column collapses to roughly 250px of empty unlabelled gutter on both tables. The Damaturu card is also clipped mid-glyph at the modal's bottom edge, pulling the eye to an unnarrated third lot at the payoff moment.
fix_recommendation: Render TECHNICAL as plain text with its scale ('91 / 100'), reserving colour for a stated threshold only, and collapse the action column when a lot is awarded so no dead gutter remains.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: The bid-comparison modal's sticky header occludes the Maiduguri lot card: the bold title '60,000 cartons RUTF delivered to Maiduguri' is entirely hidden and its subtitle is sliced mid-glyph, passing UNDER the header. This is a scroll-container layout bug, not a scroll position — and the corridor label is the load-bearing identifier for a claim that is about corridors. Secondary: 'USD' repeats in all 15 cells instead of the column header, and '.00' trails every seven-figure lot value.
fix_recommendation: Add scroll-padding-top to the modal's scroll container (or scroll-margin-top on the lot cards) equal to the sticky header height, so scroll_to lands a card's title below the header rather than under it.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: The TECHNICAL column renders a static value (91) and an interactive action ('Score') in identical teal styling, so a viewer cannot tell which cells are clickable. Every row also carries an equally prominent Award button with no selection or confirm step — 15 identical green CTAs, any of which awards the worst bid in one click. Separately, Award is live while the modal header still reads 'bids due Aug 9, 2026' and the tender status is Published.
fix_recommendation: Render scored cells as plain non-interactive text with the scale in the column header ('TECHNICAL /100'), and unscored cells as a visually distinct ghost button labelled 'Add score'.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: Every narrated claim verifies against the page — the leaders genuinely differ (Savanna 42.29 on Maiduguri, Faso 41.85 on Djibo, with Faso actually LAST at Maiduguri at 48.64), rows rank strictly by price, and all 15 unit-price x quantity products are exact. But the scene's own title asserts bids are 'scored lot by lot' while 7 of 15 rows (the Damaturu and haulage lots) carry no score at all, only a 'Score' control.
fix_recommendation: Seed BidScore rows for the Damaturu and haulage lots so the bid book is uniformly scored and the scene title is true.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: The frame is the publisher's own tender list ('Publish lots to the qualified registry, compare bids and award'); nothing on it says or shows that visibility is restricted. A cold viewer's five-second read is 'a table of six tenders', not 'eligibility is enforced' — the scene's entire claim is carried by the narrator's voice. VERIFIED: the product does have the counter-shot — static/supply/tab_supplier_home.jsx renders a 'Solicitations open to you' card with the hint 'Solicitations are visible once your organisation holds a live qualification in a matching category' — and the walkthrough already logs in as a supplier persona in scene 3, so the shot was available and not taken.
fix_recommendation: Split this into a two-beat scene: keep the publisher list, then add a beat on a supplier's home showing the 'Solicitations open to you' card, so the absence is visible rather than asserted.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers

Separately, every row carries an identical 'Compare bids' button, including the narrated row at 0/4 awarded where no bids have been compared, and five rows already Awarded — one label for three different states.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: Two action-fidelity rules fire: the narration claims an effecting act ('publishes') the trace never performs, and the sequence is illegible — four pure camera moves (nav click, wait, scroll, 3.4s hold) under a narration describing publishing a multi-lot tender. Framing itself is fine; the cursor ends parked over the '35,0' of the narrated row's Damaturu lot line.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: Two narrated elements have no on-screen referent. 'This one has dropped out because its certification lapsed last month' — no lapsed row exists; all three visible EARLIEST EXPIRY values read Feb 16/17/18 2027, roughly seven months in the future. scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen

Worse, the application opened is 'OES Supply Base 2026-A' (submitted Mar 12 2026, already Qualified), while the pending decision the narration invokes ('the decision Tomas is about to make') is on round 2026-B, submitted Jul 19 2026 — which is what scene 4 actually reviews. (b) Keep 2026-A and re-narrate so the scene is explicitly about a past, already-qualified application rather than the one about to be decided.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories

Both rounds pre-exist with IDENTICAL category sets (RUTF, Therapeutic milk, Road transport, Warehousing on both 2026-A and 2026-B), which visually argues the categories are a fixed global taxonomy rather than something Ada declares per round. (a) Perform the act on camera — click New round, name it, multi-select categories, save — noting the cost that this creates an empty round beside a populated 8-application queue. (b) Re-narrate to what is shown ('Ada's open round declares four categories, and every application in the queue is tagged against them'). Unconditionally, fix the 8-vs-4 mismatch by labelling the queue 'Showing 4 of 8 awaiting review'.
